symptom: A new lint rule's exclusion silently matched nothing. MPR019 was meant to skip attributes carrying a Unique validation rule, and kept reporting them (Mappings.Customer.CustomerId, Mappings.Order.OrderId on testdata/testapp) with the exclusion in place and its unit test green.
cause: An attribute reference arrives in TWO forms and the code assumed one. Measured on testdata/testapp: domainmodel.ValidationRule.AttributeID holds a QUALIFIED NAME ("Mappings.Order.OrderId"), while an index segment written by mxcli holds the attribute's UUID. The lookup keyed on Attribute.ID (the UUID), so the qualified-name reference never matched. Fixed with resolveAttributeRef, which accepts either: the UUID, else the last dot-segment matched against the entity's attribute names. The unit test passed throughout because it constructed the rule with a UUID, the form the code already handled.
insight: An exclusion that matches nothing is invisible: the rule keeps reporting and looks like a rule whose exclusion was unnecessary, so nothing points at the lookup. The tell was the shape of the findings, not an error — both were attributes declared `unique`, which is precisely what the exclusion was for. When an exclusion appears to be a no-op, dump the real model's reference values before trusting the unit test, because a hand-built fixture uses whichever form the author already had in mind. Model reference fields in sdk/domainmodel are NOT uniformly keyed: ValidationRule.AttributeID is by name, Index.Attributes[].AttributeID is by UUID at least when mxcli writes it, and no Studio Pro-authored index was available to confirm which form Studio Pro writes — so accept both rather than pick. Separately: a rule reading xpath_expressions must declare RequiredCatalogMode CatalogFull (the same trap MPR017 hit), and whether Mendix creates a database index to enforce `unique` was NOT established here — it decides whether excluding unique attributes is correct or merely cautious, and .claude/skills/verify-in-runtime.md plus a real database would settle it.
